channel.title: Open Calls: opportunities for journalists
channel.description: Grants, fellowships, jobs and support for journalists, checked every week.

item.title: Global Reporting Grants (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling catch-all reporting grants covering costs of in-depth stories on any topic or place; international travel awards are mostly USD 5,000 to 10,000. Open to: Staff and freelance journalists worldwide, of all nationalities: reporters, photographers, audio and video journalists, documentary filmmakers.

item.title: AI Reporting Grants (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling reporting grants for in-depth stories on AI and surveillance technologies and their impact on communities, open to journalists worldwide. Open to: Staff and freelance journalists worldwide; applications from the Global South particularly welcome.

item.title: Global Health Inequities, Risks, and Solutions (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for ambitious global health reporting, including the fallout from U.S. aid cuts, open to freelancers and newsrooms worldwide. Open to: Text, broadcast and multimedia newsrooms and freelance journalists in the U.S. and worldwide; freelancers need an outlet's commitment to publish.

item.title: Transparency & Governance Reporting Grants (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for reporting on corruption, opaque money flows and abuse of power, open to freelance and staff journalists worldwide. Open to: Freelance and staff journalists worldwide; applications from the Global South particularly welcome.

item.title: Rainforest Reporting Grant (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling, project-based funding for staff and freelance journalists reporting on tropical rainforests in the Amazon, Central Africa and Southeast Asia; applications accepted in five languages. Open to: Staff and freelance journalists reporting on tropical rainforests in the Amazon, Central Africa and Southeast Asia.

item.title: Conflict Reporting (Conflict & Peace) (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for in-depth conflict reporting, including safety costs; freelancers in war zones need an outlet's written commitment to their safety. Open to: Journalists and newsrooms covering conflict; freelancers reporting from war zones need a written assignment from an outlet taking full responsibility for their safety.

item.title: Ocean and Fisheries Reporting Grant (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for journalists worldwide to report on ocean health, illegal fishing and fisheries issues, especially from the Global South. Open to: Freelance and staff journalists from around the world; Global South applicants particularly welcome.

item.title: Climate and Labor Reporting Grants (Our Work/Environment) (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for reporting on how climate change affects workers and industries; proposals that can publish within one to four months are prioritised. Open to: U.S. residents and journalists around the world; freelance and staff journalists or groups of newsrooms.

item.title: Africa Reporting Grants (Underreported Stories in Africa) (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for journalists and newsrooms worldwide to report underreported stories affecting communities in Africa, with local journalists encouraged to apply. Open to: Newsrooms, staff and freelance journalists around the world, for stories on communities in Africa; local journalists encouraged.

item.title: U.S. Local News Reporting Grants (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for in-depth investigative and enterprise projects with local U.S. news outlets; freelancers qualify if they publish in U.S. local outlets. Open to: Freelance and staff journalists working with local U.S. news outlets; freelancers must publish in U.S. local outlets.

item.title: Machine Learning Reporting Grants (Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Rolling grants for investigations using advanced data mining such as machine learning; past awards mostly USD 10,000 to 25,000, with open methods encouraged. Open to: U.S. residents and journalists around the world; freelance data journalists, staff journalists or groups of newsrooms.

item.title: Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026 (Equality Fund)
item.description: Mentoring, a convening and reporting support for up to five journalists in aid-recipient countries covering local solutions, with a gender focus. Deadline: 2026-11-08. Open to: Full-time or freelance journalists located in and reporting on communities in ODA-recipient countries, with at least three years of experience.

item.title: German-Northern European Journalists Fellowship 2027 (International Journalists' Programmes (IJP))
item.description: Exchange fellowship placing German and Nordic/Baltic journalists in each other's newsrooms for several weeks in 2027, with a conference and a closing event in Berlin. Deadline: 2026-11-15. Open to: Journalists aged 18 to 45 working as freelancers, trainees or editors in Germany, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Estonia, Latvia or Lithuania.

item.title: WCSJ2027 Travel Fellowship (World Conference of Science Journalists 2027 (WCSJ2027))
item.description: Covers travel, visa, lodging and registration so journalists and students who cannot afford it can attend the science journalism world conference in London, September 2027. Deadline: 2026-10-23. Open to: Journalists and media professionals covering science and related fields, journalism or related students, and journalism researchers or teachers with a media track record, who need funding and can obtain a UK visa.

item.title: Fault Lines Reporting Fund (International Women's Media Foundation (IWMF))
item.description: Rolling grants for investigative US reporting on racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, misogyny and the narratives that drive hate; covers travel, security and other reporting costs. Open to: Staff and freelance journalists reporting in the United States, with 3+ years of professional experience.

item.title: MDIF Western Balkans Fund (Media Development Investment Fund (MDIF))
item.description: Standing investment fund giving loans and equity, with business advisory support, to independent media start-ups and growing outlets in the Western Balkans. Open to: Independent media companies located in or serving audiences in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia.

item.title: The Invisible Life Grant (Journalismfund Europe)
item.description: Funds cross-border investigations into farm animal welfare and related European interests, with optional mentoring; results must run in outlets in at least two countries. Deadline: 2026-10-29. Open to: Cross-border teams of at least two professional journalists and/or news outlets legally residing in at least two different countries.

item.title: Newsday/David Laventhol Visiting Professor (Columbia University Journalism School)
item.description: Full-time visiting professorship teaching reporting courses and advising master's projects for the 2027-28 academic year, renewable once; expertise in diversity-in-media reporting expected. Open to: Must currently hold an appointment at another academic institution; bachelor's degree required.

item.title: Africa Broadcast Producer (Bloomberg)
item.description: Experienced television producer in Johannesburg shaping Bloomberg Television's Africa coverage: breaking news, live shows, interviews and features; five or more years of TV experience asked.

item.title: Program Coordinator, AI Initiative (The Pulitzer Center)
item.description: Administrative role running the Pulitzer Center's AI journalism network: newsletter, trainings, grant paperwork and payments; English plus one of its other programme languages. Open to: Fully remote, open to candidates located anywhere in the world.

item.title: Asia Editor (Semafor)
item.description: Senior editor leading Semafor's Asia coverage and building its reporting team, with a business and finance focus; ten-plus years of journalism and newsroom leadership asked. Open to: Remote; ideal candidate based in Singapore, open to applicants elsewhere in the region.

item.title: Bilingual Editor (Palestine Reporting Lab)
item.description: One-year contract as the lead Arabic-language editor for investigative and narrative journalism on Palestine; five years of journalism experience asked, extension possible. Open to: Can be based anywhere, but must be willing to hold meetings during US and Palestine working hours.

item.title: Writer (Our World in Data)
item.description: Senior writer producing data-driven articles on global problems for a general audience; hiring starts with a paid two-article writing residency before any offer. Open to: International applicants welcome; working hours should partly overlap with UK hours; visa sponsorship may be considered.

item.title: Reporting Fellowships for Journalists to Cover BBNJ COP1 in New York City, USA (Internews' Earth Journalism Network)
item.description: EJN will fund ten journalists to report from the first High Seas Treaty conference in New York in January 2027, covering travel and stay. Deadline: 2026-10-27. Open to: Professional journalists from or representing an established media house and reporting from a coastal country; freelancers need a letter of support from an outlet.

item.title: Virtual Media Workshops on the 30x30 Target and Marine Protected Areas 2027 (Internews' Earth Journalism Network)
item.description: Three-day online workshops for journalists in Ghana, Mexico and the Philippines on marine protected areas, with a path to later story grants. Deadline: 2026-11-02. Open to: Journalists, content creators and other media practitioners from Ghana, Mexico or the Philippines.

item.title: Text and Video Reports on Renewable Energy in India (Internews' Earth Journalism Network)
item.description: Grants for communicators and social media creators in India to produce text or video reports on the renewable energy transition, with editorial mentoring. Deadline: 2026-11-15. Open to: Communicators and social media content creators based anywhere in India, with preference for Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh.

item.title: 2027 Safety Ambassador Fellowship (International Women's Media Foundation (IWMF))
item.description: Six-month programme training U.S. journalists as newsroom Safety Ambassadors, with expert mentoring and a small stipend, then four trainings delivered afterwards. Deadline: 2026-10-19. Open to: Journalists based in the U.S. who work in journalism, especially local newsrooms; open to all genders.

item.title: ODA Germany Grants, Round 2: reporting on maternal and child health (European Journalism Centre (EJC))
item.description: Grants for reporting on maternal and child health and German development aid, to be published in German media by 30 April 2027. Deadline: 2026-10-23. Open to: Germany-based freelance journalists, independent or regional German media, news creators, or teams including a Germany-based journalist or German media partner.

item.title: Technology Journalism Fellowship 2027 (Publix, House for Journalism and the Public Sphere)
item.description: Four-week fellowship in two phases (April and September 2027) for six journalists on digital sovereignty, with expert meetings in Berlin and Brussels. Deadline: 2026-11-15. Open to: Tech, digital, politics, business and science journalists, freelance or employed, living in Germany or Switzerland who speak German and English.

item.title: Research travel scholarship for journalists from North Rhine-Westphalia (Stipendium für Journalisten aus NRW) (Heinz-Kühn-Stiftung)
item.description: Six-week or three-month research trip to Africa, Asia or Latin America on a self-chosen topic, with flat-rate funding and a research report afterwards. Deadline: 2026-11-30. Open to: Young journalists from North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, aged 35 or under, with journalism training begun or several years of journalism work.

item.title: Future Journalist Program (RTDNA Canada)
item.description: Canadian programme giving selected journalism students CTV newsroom tours, interviews with veteran journalists, career workshops and an awards gala ticket. Deadline: 2026-12-15. Open to: Post-secondary journalism and media students.

item.title: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships at Stanford 2027-28 (John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships, Stanford University)
item.description: Nine-month residential fellowship at Stanford (September to May) for experienced journalists to pursue a question about journalism, with coaching and a global alumni network. Deadline: 2026-12-02. Open to: Journalists and people working in service of journalism with at least five years' professional experience, employed or freelance; citizens of countries under a US J-visa suspension cannot be offered a fellowship.

item.title: GIJC27 Fellowship (Global Investigative Journalism Conference 2027) (Global Investigative Journalism Network (GIJN), co-host VVOJ)
item.description: Funded places at the Global Investigative Journalism Conference in Rotterdam, October 2027, covering flights, hotel and registration, prioritising Global South and underrepresented journalists. Deadline: 2027-01-31. Open to: Professional journalists, including freelancers, prioritising the Global South and historically underrepresented groups; others who cannot cover the cost may apply too.

item.title: True Story Award 2027 (True Story Foundation (True Story Festival))
item.description: International award for published long-form reports (15,000 to 85,000 characters) in Research, Storytelling and Impact categories, with USD 20,000 per winner. Deadline: 2026-10-31. Open to: Journalists from around the world; text reports published between 1 October 2025 and 30 September 2026.

item.title: 2026 Lauren Brown Fellowship (International Women's Media Foundation (IWMF))
item.description: Grants of up to USD 2,000 for U.S.-based women and nonbinary journalists from underrepresented backgrounds to fund reporting projects or professional development. Deadline: 2026-10-30. Open to: Women and nonbinary journalists from underrepresented backgrounds, based in the U.S..

item.title: Freelancer Support Scheme (IJ4EU (run by the European Journalism Centre))
item.description: Grants for cross-border investigations by teams of freelancers, with mentoring, training and networking; the next call opens on 1 December 2026. Open to: Cross-border teams of at least two freelance journalists, based in at least two Creative Europe countries.

item.title: Investigation Support Scheme (IJ4EU (run by the International Press Institute))
item.description: Funding for cross-border investigative projects in Europe, open to newsroom and freelance teams; the next call opens on 1 December 2026. Open to: Cross-border teams of journalists and/or news organisations based in at least two Creative Europe countries.

item.title: Institutional Grants (Tarbell Center for AI Journalism)
item.description: Large grants to news outlets and teams to build AI reporting capacity, including new units, series or ventures, with an open round now running. Deadline: 2026-12-11. Open to: Media outlets and teams, nonprofit or for-profit, building AI reporting capacity.

item.title: Journalists-in-Residence (European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF))
item.description: Three to six months of safe shelter in Leipzig for journalists under threat, with stipend, housing, insurance and optional counselling and training. Open to: Threatened journalists, media workers, documentarists and press photographers; legal residents of EU member or candidate states, Council of Europe states, or Belarus/Russia; English, German or Russian at A2.

item.title: Journalists-in-Exile Programme (European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF))
item.description: ECPMF arranges and pays for training, language courses, legal advice, therapy and equipment to help exiled journalists in Germany keep working. Open to: Media professionals in exile in Germany, regardless of origin, who had to leave their country because of oppression or persecution.

item.title: SAFE Psychological Support Fund (European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF), SAFE project)
item.description: Small grants to pay for therapy or counselling for journalists in five Eastern Partnership countries, for care completed by 31 December 2026. Deadline: 2026-11-15. Open to: Journalists and media workers at editorially independent outlets covering Ukraine, Moldova, Armenia, Azerbaijan or Georgia.

item.title: Practical support (European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF), with Free Press Unlimited via MFRR)
item.description: Short-term emergency help for threatened journalists, covering medical costs, subsistence, therapy, safety tools and family support, applied for through Reporters Respond. Open to: Media organisations and practising media professionals in an EU member or candidate state facing an emergency caused by their work.

item.title: 2027 Ochberg Fellowships (Global Center for Journalism & Trauma (GCJT))
item.description: A week-long seminar in Paris (22-27 March 2027) on trauma and ethical reporting on violence and conflict, with travel and lodging paid. Deadline: 2026-10-20. Open to: Mid- and senior-career journalists from any part of the world with at least five years of professional experience; students are not eligible.

item.title: Outrider Foundation: story pitches on nuclear risk and climate change (Outrider Foundation)
item.description: Standing invitation to pitch narrative stories on nuclear threats and climate change; accepted pieces of roughly 1,000 to 1,200 words are paid per story.

item.title: Fund for Investigative Journalism: Regular and Seed Grants (winter 2027 round) (Fund for Investigative Journalism)
item.description: Grants for US-focused investigative reporting costs such as travel, records and reporting time, with small seed grants for early groundwork. Deadline: 2027-01-29. Open to: Freelance journalists, staff reporters and media outlets; foreign-based proposals need a strong U.S. angle and a U.S. outlet.

item.title: SJN/MIT Climate Journalism Fellowship 2027 (Solutions Journalism Network with MIT)
item.description: Eight-month fellowship, January to August 2027, for ten US journalists to report local climate solutions stories, with training, coaching and a stipend. Deadline: 2026-10-26. Open to: Freelance and staff journalists based in the U.S., with interest from a local or regional news outlet to publish the project.

item.title: AI-Assisted Data Journalism (online masterclass) (Arena for Journalism in Europe)
item.description: Three live two-hour sessions teaching journalists to use local AI coding agents for cleaning data, analysis and scraping, with homework between sessions. Deadline: 2026-11-15. Open to: Reporters, editors and researchers with some experience in data analysis (know what a pivot table is); no coding experience required.

item.title: Hans Staiger Investigative Reporting Award 2027 (International Center for Journalists (ICFJ), with OCCRP)
item.description: One $5,000 award a year funds an OCCRP-network journalist's investigative project, with OCCRP help on research, editing, fact-checking and legal review. Deadline: 2026-11-15. Open to: Journalists in the global network of the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP).

item.title: Nieman Fellowships at Harvard (2027-28 class) (Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard)
item.description: Academic-year fellowship at Harvard where about two dozen journalists study, audit classes and join a cohort, including an innovation track with the Berkman Klein Center. Deadline: 2026-12-01. Open to: Working journalists with at least five years of full-time media experience, from any country.

item.title: The Stringer Awards 2027 (The Stringer Foundation)
item.description: Unrestricted multi-year cash awards for journalists who expose abuses of power, with vetted applicants also offered safety, mental health, publication and legal support. Deadline: 2026-12-31. Open to: Journalists and creative practitioners across all public media forms, senior and emerging, who expose abuses of power; applications may be written in your own language.

item.title: Gordon N. Fisher / Journalists for Human Rights Fellowship (Massey College, University of Toronto, with Journalists for Human Rights)
item.description: A year of study at the University of Toronto for one journalist from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East, with monthly stipend and airfare. Deadline: 2026-12-01. Open to: One journalist from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East, fluent in written and spoken English, with at least seven years of journalism experience.

item.title: Knight-Wallace Fellowships 2027-2028 (international applicants) (Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan)
item.description: Academic-year fellowship in Ann Arbor for experienced journalists to pursue a project; international applicants apply separately from U.S. citizens, with offers by mid-February 2027. Deadline: 2026-12-01. Open to: Non-U.S. citizens with at least five years of experience, working in journalism for a news organisation or independently.

item.title: Early-Career Fellowship Program (The Open Notebook)
item.description: Paid, part-time 12-month remote fellowship where early-career science journalists work with a mentor to report and publish articles for The Open Notebook, starting February 2027. Deadline: 2026-10-31. Open to: Early-career science journalists with fewer than three years of regular professional experience writing about science for the public; applicants outside the U.S. welcome.

item.title: Bilingual International Journalism Traineeship (DW Akademie (Deutsche Welle))
item.description: Salaried 18-month bilingual German-English journalism traineeship at DW, with twelve places for aspiring journalists from around the world, applied for via an online portal. Deadline: 2026-11-17. Open to: People with a university degree in any subject and journalistic experience or a wish to switch to journalism; German and English are both mandatory; no age limit.

item.title: Researcher, North Africa (Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ))
item.description: Fully remote role documenting press freedom violations and attacks on journalists in North Africa, writing alerts and reports, and vetting journalist assistance requests. Deadline: 2026-10-23. Open to: Mid-level researchers based in North Africa, the Middle East or a similar time zone (such as Europe); able to translate between Arabic and English.

item.title: Spanish editor (The European Correspondent)
item.description: Part-time freelance editor who translates and edits the outlet's newsletters, social posts and videos into Spanish and builds engagement campaigns for Spanish-speaking readers. Open to: Native Spanish speakers with excellent English and at least a year in Spanish-language media; must be a registered freelancer in an EU country.

item.title: Freelance Researcher (women's financial equality) (The Fawcett Society)
item.description: Short freelance research contract alongside the charity's investigative researcher on women's working and financial lives, remote within the UK, starting immediately. Deadline: 2026-10-20. Open to: Established researchers with rigorous research skills and an investigative instinct; background may be research, journalism, policy or campaigning.

item.title: Feature Writer (freelance) (How-To Geek (Valnet Publishing Group))
item.description: Remote 1099 freelance role writing how-to guides, tutorials and explainers on hardware, operating systems, mobile and smart home topics, chosen from a pool of assignments. Open to: Experienced tech writers with 1+ year of relevant experience writing and editing English tech content; must work reliably within a US time zone; not a news-writing role.

item.title: English Desk Editor (Bangkok / Hong Kong / Los Angeles / Washington) (Agence France-Presse (AFP))
item.description: Permanent editing posts on AFP's English-language news desks in Asia and North America, which can lead to reporting assignments and correspondent postings. Open to: Experienced journalists with at least three years of editorial experience, preferably in both reporting and editing; willing to work any shift and weekends.

item.title: Journaliste rédacteur.rice arabophone (France 24 (France Médias Monde))
item.description: Freelance web journalist writing in literary Arabic for a France Medias Monde information portal aimed at migrants, producing text, social posts and mobile video. Open to: Journalists with literary Arabic and fluent French, with web newsroom experience.

item.title: How to Pitch Nieman Reports (Nieman Reports (Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard))
item.description: Open pitching for reported features of 1,200 to 3,000 words and opinion columns on challenges, trends and craft in journalism today.

item.title: Video Pitches (Mongabay)
item.description: Mongabay takes pitches for short environmental documentaries and vertical news videos, preferring early-stage proposals with shot list, timeline and budget. Open to: Experienced video journalists, producers, DPs, editors, animators.

item.title: Reporting Grants to Amplify Caregiving Stories (New America, Better Life Lab)
item.description: Funding, editing and placement help for solutions stories about child care and the wider care system, mainly in the US, in any medium. Open to: New and experienced journalists and storytellers; people with underrepresented perspectives especially encouraged.

item.title: Pitch call: "Automation" theme, May/June 2027 issue (MIT Technology Review)
item.description: Feature pitches of 2,500 to 4,000 words for the magazine's Automation issue: narrative features, investigations, profiles and reported essays. Open to: Freelance writers of all levels and backgrounds; writers from outside the United States especially welcome.

item.title: RSF assistance to journalists and media (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: RSF offers journalists and media travel insurance, protective-gear loans, emergency financial and administrative aid and asylum support; not every request can be met. Open to: Journalists of all nationalities facing critical situations, journalists in exile, and local media or press freedom organisations; RSF cannot grant every request.

item.title: RSF Digital Security Lab (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: Forensic service that checks journalists' devices and accounts for malware, phishing and account takeovers; it cannot provide incident response or prove a device is clean. Open to: Journalists affected by, or with good reason to believe they have suffered, a digital attack; priority is given to cases meeting set criteria, others only if capacity allows.

item.title: RSF security training programme for Hong Kong journalists (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: Digital and physical security training for Hong Kong media and independent journalists, in groups of 15 to 25; register through the site's contact form. Open to: Hong Kong media outlets and independent journalists, professional and non-professional; the planning team selects participants by profile and need.

item.title: Reporter ohne Grenzen support for journalists [Unterstützung für Journalist*innen] (Reporter ohne Grenzen (RSF Germany))
item.description: Emergency administrative and financial aid for journalists under threat worldwide, with help in exile; it also runs Berlin fellowships for at-risk journalists. Open to: Threatened journalists and media workers worldwide whose threat or persecution is a direct result of their reporting.

item.title: Freelance editors-in-chief, journalists and copy editors [Rédacteurs en chef, journalistes et secrétaires de rédaction pigistes] (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: RSF seeks freelance editors-in-chief, reporters and French/English copy editors for its press-freedom publications; apply by email with CV and letter, reference PIGES. Open to: Freelance editors-in-chief (3+ years' experience), journalists (3+ years in journalism) and French/English copy editors (2+ years); fluent English required.

item.title: Editorial Directorate intern, English-language content [Stagiaire à la direction éditoriale - attaché-e à l’édition des contenus anglophones] (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: Four-to-six-month internship in RSF's Paris editorial department, translating and editing journalistic content from French into English and helping with newsletters. Open to: Students in journalism, translation, communication or similar (Bac+3 to Bac+5); native English speaker with at least B2 French; internship agreement required.

item.title: Middle East bureau intern [Stagiaire au bureau Moyen-Orient] (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: Six-month full-time internship at RSF's Middle East bureau in Paris, monitoring press freedom in 15 countries, verifying information and writing dispatches; Arabic required. Open to: Students of journalism, political science, international studies, Arabic or related subjects; fluent Arabic plus French and/or English; full-time, no parallel classes; internship agreement required.

item.title: Emergency Response and Security Officer, Dakar [Chargé.e de réponse aux urgences et sécurité], ref. Crises Dakar 26 (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: Fixed-term post at RSF's Sub-Saharan Africa bureau in Dakar, coordinating emergency responses for journalists and media and managing security of RSF staff and activities. Deadline: 2026-10-20. Open to: Degree in international relations, political or social sciences, security or equivalent; 5+ years in international project management and/or emergency security; English required, French a plus.

item.title: Public tender: Journalism Trust Initiative Fast Track Program in Estonia (Reporters Without Borders (RSF))
item.description: Service providers are sought to help at least ten Estonian media outlets publish Journalism Trust Initiative transparency reports over four months from mid-November 2026. Deadline: 2026-11-06. Open to: Service-provider organisations (not individual freelancers) with expertise in the Estonian media landscape and in training and capacity building for journalists and media; registration certificate required.
